content.value_statement: Remotion upgrades can leave packages and lockfiles out of sync. This skill guides a consistent upgrade for Remotion, Mediabunny, and installed Remotion skills.
actual_capabilities: Inspects manifests and lockfiles to identify the package manager and workspace structure.
Uses the local Remotion CLI upgrade workflow when the CLI is available.
Finds installed Remotion packages and aligns them to one stable version.
Checks the documented Mediabunny compatibility version before updating related packages.
Updates the lockfile through the project package manager.
Reviews dependency changes and verifies installed Remotion versions.
limitations: It only upgrades dependencies already present in the project.
It depends on current Remotion documentation and package registry availability.
It does not guarantee application behavior after a major version upgrade.
It does not replace project-specific tests or manual review of breaking changes.

use_cases.title: Update a production video project
use_cases.description: Align Remotion and Mediabunny versions before releasing an updated video application.

use_cases.title: Maintain a monorepo workspace
use_cases.description: Upgrade Remotion dependencies consistently across workspace packages while preserving existing dependency conventions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a dependency maintenance change
use_cases.description: Create a focused Remotion upgrade and lockfile update that reviewers can inspect clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Upgrade my project
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade this Remotion project to the latest stable compatible versions. Inspect the manifests and lockfile first, then review the changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A single-package Remotion project needs routine maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Preserve workspace conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade all Remotion and compatible Mediabunny packages in this workspace. Preserve dependency sections, workspace conventions, and unrelated changes.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Verify version alignment
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade this Remotion project, update installed Remotion skills, and verify that every Remotion package uses one version. Summarize relevant release changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer needs an auditable upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Plan a controlled upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository and propose a controlled Remotion upgrade. Identify affected packages, compatible Mediabunny versions, validation steps, and breaking-change risks before editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a reviewable upgrade plan.

output_examples.input: Upgrade this Remotion project to current compatible packages.
output: Identified the package manager and installed Remotion packages.
Updated Remotion packages to one stable version.
Selected the documented compatible Mediabunny version.
Updated the lockfile and summarized the dependency diff.

output_examples.input: Check whether our workspace has aligned Remotion versions.
output: Found Remotion packages across workspace manifests.
Reported packages that use a different version.
Recommended a single target version and validation command.

best_practices: Review manifest and lockfile changes before committing the upgrade.
Run the project test and render checks after dependency updates.
Read release notes when upgrading across major versions.
anti_patterns: Do not upgrade only one Remotion package when related packages are installed.
Do not select a Mediabunny version without checking the compatibility documentation.
Do not discard unrelated dependency or lockfile changes.

faq.question: What does this skill upgrade?
faq.answer: It upgrades installed Remotion packages, compatible Mediabunny packages, and installed Remotion skills.

faq.question: Does it use the Remotion CLI?
faq.answer: It uses the local Remotion CLI upgrade workflow when the CLI is available.

faq.question: How does it handle Mediabunny?
faq.answer: It checks the Remotion compatibility documentation and updates installed Mediabunny packages to the compatible version.

faq.question: Will it change unrelated dependencies?
faq.answer: The instructions say to preserve unrelated changes and existing dependency conventions.

faq.question: Does it update the lockfile?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs the project package manager to update the lockfile after dependency changes.

faq.question: Does it validate my application?
faq.answer: It checks dependency alignment, but you must run project-specific tests and render checks.
